label: AI Energy Bills
title: AI Energy Consumption: The Hidden Cost of Intelligence
body:
AI systems consume real electricity every time you send a prompt. According to OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, a single ChatGPT query uses about 0.34 watt-hours — roughly what a high-efficiency lightbulb uses in a couple of minutes. That sounds tiny, but multiply it by billions of daily queries and the numbers get serious fast.

The energy cost happens at two stages: training (the one-time process of building the model) and inference (every time someone actually uses it). Training a model like GPT-4 reportedly consumed around 50-60 gigawatt-hours — enough to power thousands of homes for a year. But inference energy now adds up even faster because usage never stops.

At the global level, AI is reshaping power grids. Data centers consumed about 415 terawatt-hours in 2024 — roughly 1.5% of global electricity. The International Energy Agency projects this could more than double to 945 TWh by 2030, with AI as a primary driver. Tech companies are now racing to secure nuclear power deals just to keep their servers running.
